newsitem.title: UK: HGCA sees enough malting barley for domestic use.
newsitem.headline: HGCA sees enough malting barley for domestic use.

text.p: Malting barley supplies in the UK may be less tight than previously expected, a factor that has pressured prices recently, the Home-Grown Cereals Authority (HGCA) said on Wednesday.

The Ministry of Agriculture (MAFF) has recently forecast domestic usage of malting barley at nearly two million tonnes this season against an estimated production of low nitrogen varieties of 1.9 million tonnes.

Malting barley types recommended by the Institute of Brewing (IOB) were estimated to have increased by 200,000 tonnes this year to 3.0 million tonnes after an increase in sowings and yields this year.
Brewers usually favour crops with nitrogen content of less than 1.8 percent, but changing demand trends such as a rise in lager consumption mean nitrogen up to 1.85 is now becoming acceptable.

Some 200,000 tonnes of malting barley could be designated for food malt which can also use non-IOB varieties and supplies could be further improved by blending the high and low nitrogen types, the HGCA said.
In addition, maltsters were believed to have carried an extra 100,000 tonnes of stocks over from the last season.
"These factors suggest the supply situation for malting barley is less tight than the estimated supply of low nitrogen barley suggests," it said in a weekly report.
HGCA expected the domestic market to absorb the majority of malting barley with export demand falling due to large crops in Europe and the rest of the world.
